description: Fix security vulnerabilities: 32 npm audit findings (3 Critical, 22 High, 7 Moderate) including Next.js CVE, deprecated packages, and implement missing security headers.
steps: Review npm audit output for the 32 vulnerabilities, focusing on Critical (Next.js 14.2.15) and High severity issues.
Update package.json dependencies: next@14.2.15 → latest 14.x or 15.x stable (check breaking changes), eslint@8.57.1 → 9.x, recharts@2.13.0 → latest stable.
Run npm update to apply safe updates for transitive dependencies.

Add security headers in next.config.js or middleware: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy.
Add middleware.ts at root to set security headers on all responses.
Verify CSRF protection in server actions (Next.js 14 has built-in CSRF for server actions via origin check).
Add rate limiting middleware wrapper for API routes in lib/api.ts using existing rate-limit utility.
Document security headers in docs/SECURITY.md update.
Run npm audit to verify Critical and High vulnerabilities are resolved (acceptable: Moderate with documented mitigation).
Run npm run build to ensure no breaking changes from updates.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit shows 0 Critical, 0 High vulnerabilities (Moderate acceptable with plan)
Security headers present in all responses (verify with curl or browser devtools)
Next.js updated to patched version without breaking changes
Rate limiting applied to sensitive API endpoints
All tests still pass after dependency updates
verification: curl -I http://localhost:3000 | grep -E '(X-Frame-Options|X-Content-Type-Options|Referrer-Policy)' to verify headers after starting dev server
findings: 32 security vulnerabilities including Next.js CVE. No security headers configured. CSRF relies on Next.js built-in but not explicitly documented. Rate limiting exists but not applied to API routes. Deprecated packages: eslint@8, glob@7, recharts@2.x branches inactive.
